newsitem.title: UK: London gold fixes easier, watches dollar moves.
newsitem.headline: London gold fixes easier, watches dollar moves.

text.p: Precious metal prices were mostly lower in Europe on Friday following selling and long liquidation as the dollar strengthened late Thursday.
The dollar move followed another set of benign inflation data which also brought strength to the U.S. stocks and bonds markets.
"The stronger dollar meant gold prices rose in the other major currencies which stopped any buying but also brought out producer selling and long liquidation," a dealer said.
Gold was fixed at $323.50 per ounce against $326.15 on Thursday after marking a slip back to near the bottom end of the $323-$328 trading range which has prevailed all week.
Business was quiet in Europe with large parts of continental Europe observing Assumption Day and dealers said any serious move away from the fixing level was unlikely until the U.S. markets opened.
A bounce to $326.00 was conceivable then but if the financial markets firmed again $321-$322 could be tested, dealers said.
Although prices were easier in Asia following liquidation and fresh shorts opening in New York, physical offtake was in reasonable volume, they said.
Lease rates continued to firm with the implied one-month level at 2.73 percent up five basis points from Thursday and the further out rates with the exception of the 12-month rate were also higher.
Rates had been easier early and overnight after the rise of around 40 basis points on Thursday attracted fresh lending to the market.
"It has the feel of producer selling rather than central bank selling," one dealers said of the rising rate pattern.
"When a central bank comes it usually reflects in rises only in the near-by dates," he added.

Silver was eight cents lower at $4.41/$4.43 losing ground with gold and was very quiet having disappointed supporters after its attempts to establish itself above $4.50 failed on Wednesday and Thursday.
Platinum was indicated at $422.00/$425.00 down $2.50. Some dealers said unconfirmed talk of Russian spot selling in Europe was behind the easier tone.
"But spreads are still so wide that a $10 move in a few minutes is nothing," a dealer said.
